title: A look at SOAP and integration with legacy systems

videos.script: Behind a lot of shops there is an older system. A bank, a tax authority, a warehouse. It has worked for twenty years, and nobody is going to rewrite it. {{legacy}} Many of those systems speak SOAP. Every message is XML, wrapped in an envelope, sent over HTTP. And there is a contract that a program can read. {{envelope}} The bookshop in this course buys from a distributor like that. You cannot reach the real one from here. So you run a stand-in for it, on your own machine, and it speaks the same way. {{standin}} First you read its contract, and you call it by hand with curl. Then you let a library build the client from the contract, and you see what that costs. {{client}} Then the part that matters most. You put an adapter between the shop and the old system. The shop never learns the old system's words. {{bridge}} And at the end you make the distributor slow, on purpose. A timeout tells you that you stopped waiting. It does not tell you what happened on the other side. {{timeout}}
